The broker relationship: which partner desk executes orders.
The asset list: how many pairs are actually offered.
The registration flow: what personal details the form collects.
The risk disclosure: where the capital-at-risk wording sits.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Enter your name, email, phone and country, then confirm through the emailed link.

steps.title: Fund
steps.text: Send the US$300 starting deposit through one of the accepted methods.

steps.title: Configure
steps.text: Adjust the risk controls, pick a mode and practise on the demo before going live.

pros: Funding by card, transfer, PayPal and Skrill.
cons: Asset list that shifts between pages.
The headline fee claim and the real cost disagree.
redFlags: Restriction lists that name different countries.
Payout promises with no processing detail.
No regulator, licence or audit named anywhere.

faqs.q: What does the published score actually mean?
faqs.a: It does double duty - a platform score and an early community response - and neither is independently verified. Treat both as marketing until proven otherwise.
Yes - signup is free and activates through a confirmation link. The first cost is the US$300 deposit, which stays in your trading balance.
The platform fee is absent, but every trade carries a broker spread the page itself calls the real cost. The headline says free; the fine print says otherwise. Budget for the fine print.

faqs.q: How much support does it offer?
faqs.a: Unclear - around-the-clock coverage is claimed, while other sections quote different figures. Ask support to reconcile them before you fund anything.
Yes - the platform offers automatic and manual modes, so you can follow the signals or confirm each entry yourself.

bottomLine: The desk, the demo and the funding options all check out. The score reflects the paperwork around them.
Our 4.7 reflects what the pages publish and what they skip. It is not a warning off - it is a reminder to trade the product, not the pitch.
